data.title: Microsoft ‘deeply sorry’ as outage triggers global chaos
data.description:
Microsoft on Nov 13 apologised for a global outage that disrupted public services and businesses around the world, as it reported a “broad recovery” for Outlook email and other services.

The company ruled out any malicious “cyber or AI” activity as the cause of the outage, which affected several Microsoft products and disrupted health care services, delayed corporate earnings reports and left schools struggling to communicate.

“We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners,” Microsoft said on X, adding full services were still being restored after the outage started on Nov 12.

“We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services. This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents.”

The disruption knocked out Microsoft products in 74 countries and territories, affecting users across the Americas and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa, according to the outage tracker Downdetector.

A top UK trade union said the disruptions had a “serious impact” on the country’s health care service.

National Health Service staff receiving emergency calls were “unable to refer patient details in the normal way,” creating a massive backlog, said Rachel Harrison, public services head at the GMB union.

As the outage dragged on for hours, airlines in India warned that customer queries may not be getting through.

IndiGo and Akasa Air both said on X that their email support services had been affected and that they may not be able to receive customers’ emails.

Immigration New Zealand said the disruption had forced a halt in the processing of all visa applications.

‘Significant impact’

Japan’s economy, trade and industry minister Ryosei Akazawa warned of a “significant impact” of the outage as the Microsoft products were used by a “vast number of people.”

In London’s financial district, several people interviewed by AFP said the outage exposed their dependence on Copilot, Microsoft’s AI assistant.

“I think one of the biggest things is Copilot not working,” said Yashmit Sharma, 26, an auditor. “I think this was the main bummer. And Outlook as well, of course.”

Sheera, 40, a risk manager at a mid-sized bank, said businesses needed to be better prepared for unexpected technology failures.

“I think we need to be a little bit more careful,” said Sheera, declining to give her last name. “Anything can happen: you wake up and Outlook is not working and it’s the main communication we use for our global team.”

The Australian Computer Society (ACS) called for a national review of sovereign IT risk, with CEO Prins Ralston saying that small businesses may not have a workaround when Outlook fails.

“We need to know the systems that keep this country running won’t simply fall over without notice,” Ralston said, according to ACS publication Information Age.

On Nov 12, Microsoft attributed the disruption to “elevated load” on its infrastructure.

In an updated statement on Friday, it said the “incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change.”

“We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.”

Reports of problems on Downdetector had begun to decline by 9am GMT (5pm Singapore time).

Microsoft initially said it was investigating outage reports “in the Americas,” but later confirmed that the issue apparently affected “Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region.”

Microsoft 365 is the company’s cloud-based subscription service that includes popular applications such as Outlook and Teams. AFP

data.title: Nvidia approached Arm CEO Rene Haas to succeed Jensen Huang, report says
data.description:
Nvidia’s board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang, the Financial Times reported on Nov 13, citing people familiar with the matter.

Huang stepped down on Nov 12 after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, plunging the chipmaker into crisis and sending shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll.

Haas’ name has been making the rounds among analysts since Huang’s exit. He spent seven formative years at Nvidia, rising to vice-president and general manager of its computing products business, before joining Arm in 2013.

He is among several candidates being considered and there is no guarantee he will be offered the job or accept it, the FT reported. Nvidia’s finance chief Colette Kress is currently interim CEO.

Arm declined to comment, while Nvidia did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Reuters could not independently verify the report.

Haas became Arm CEO in 2022, overseeing the company’s Nasdaq listing in 2023. Arm designs processor architectures and licences them to other companies that develop chip designs. Historically its strength has been in mobile phones and it is expanding into computers.

Arm’s US-listed shares pared losses after the report and were down more than 5%. Nvidia’s shares were down over 3%.

Some analysts expect the next CEO to break from Huang’s three-decade reign as the hands-on “chief conductor” who personally steered engineering roadmaps, geopolitical negotiations over China exports and massive investments across the AI ecosystem.

A potential shift toward a more institutional leadership structure would come as Nvidia faces heightened regulatory scrutiny and growing consensus among US lawmakers to further restrict the company’s chip exports to China.

Insiders and tech titans in the running

Analysts view Kress as a steady financial authority, while veteran engineer Ian Buck is seen as a top candidate after leading development of CUDA, the software platform that powers Nvidia’s AI chips.

Apart from Haas, external names discussed by analysts include AMD chief Lisa Su, who has navigated the key China market, and Micron chief Sanjay Mehrotra, whose memory chips power Nvidia servers.

Other candidates cited by industry watchers include Marvell head Matt Murphy and Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, who oversaw the iPhone maker’s in-house silicon development.

Former Apple chief Tim Cook was floated by US President Donald Trump, as Nvidia’s board evaluates whether to prioritise financial continuity, deep technical expertise, or experience running a global tech heavyweight. REUTERS

data.title: Genting Singapore shares fall as high rollers play less, resort revamp continues
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Shares of Genting Singapore were down by more than 6% at 57 cents at noon on Nov 13, after the company reported another quarter of shrinking profits, as high rollers played less at Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) and ongoing renovations at the resort crimped visitor footfall and spending.

Net profit fell 42% year on year to $54.7 million for the three months ended Sept 30, while revenue fell 13% to $566.1 million, Genting Singapore said in a business update on Nov 12.

Both net profit and revenue for the July to September quarter were also lower than in the previous quarter from April to June.

Casino revenue fell 22% to $315 million for the quarter under review compared with a year ago, as lower activity among premium gamblers and a lower-than-usual share of wagers retained by the casino in September further dented revenue. However, Genting said this was in line with trends in key regional markets.

The group said adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation for the quarter, a measure of operating performance, would have been about $36 million higher than the reported $161.8 million if the casino had kept its usual share of premium wagers.

Outside the casino, non-gaming revenue rose 1% year on year to $250.9 million for the quarter, despite fewer hotel rooms being available.

This was up 29% from the previous quarter, although Genting did not elaborate on what drove the increase.

The resort operator is banking on the year-end holiday season to draw visitors, even as upgrades to its hotels, gaming areas and other guest spaces limit how much of the resort it can operate through 2027.

As part of efforts to attract premium customers, the resort is stepping up its marketing and using events and new openings at Weave, its retail and dining precinct, to give guests more reasons to visit.

At the same time, RWS is revamping its gaming areas, lounges, restaurants and other guest spaces.

It expects the upgrades to improve its hotel offerings and broaden the resort’s appeal over the longer term.

data.title: Binance finishes covering US$6.3 billion of stolen customer tokens
data.description:
Binance said it has covered all US$6.3 billion (S$8.1 billion) in crypto assets pilfered from customers, marking a capstone to the largest cybertheft in history.

The Oct 29 incident, which the US government and analysts have blamed on North Korea, involved not just common cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin, but more obscure tokens that took Binance more time to find and purchase.

As at Nov 12, the crypto exchange had restored all of them, according to a social media post. 

“To our users and community: thank you for your patience and understanding,” Binance said in its post on social media platform X.

Binance spent a mixture of its profits and other emergency funds to quickly restore most of the stolen tokens in a matter of days, but said a remaining 10% would require more effort.

It pledged throughout the process to completely cover lost funds.

Hackers used a maze of tools to launder the cryptocurrencies stolen from Binance, including transferring the tokens through thousands of digital wallets and across multiple blockchains in an effort to obscure their origins.

The thieves used meme-coins to launder a slice of the proceeds, allowing them to pass through about US$430,000 of the stolen crypto.

The automated nature of the transactions was also notable.

Within a week of the hack, the laundering effort used more than 20,000 wallets and executed at least 65,000 transactions, according to blockchain analytics firm Elliptic.

That equates to roughly one new wallet being used every 30 seconds and one transaction completed every 10 seconds.

Blockchain security firm Chainalysis also recently highlighted the role of Chinese money-laundering networks in cashing out the funds.

The enormous cyberheist of the world’s largest crypto exchange came at a time when the digital asset industry is pushing ever more into mainstream finance.

It also highlighted the prevalence of cybersecurity challenges – especially since a key vulnerability appears to have been an engineer who was phished through a phoney job offer.

Crypto exchanges Bitget and Bybit, as well as companies that helped keep tokens safe with physical hardware, such as Coinkite and Ledger, have all also experienced major incidents recently. BLOOMBERG

data.title: New business-class seats, Air India plans among key takeaways from SIA’s first-half results briefing
data.description:
SINGAPORE – A week after receiving mixed feedback on its newly unveiled business-class seats, Singapore Airlines chief executive Goh Choon Phong said the airline would explore the possibility of making adjustments where it deemed fit.

Without elaborating on the extent of any possible changes, Goh said at SIA’s results briefing on Nov 12 that the group acknowledges the feedback it had received and would review it so that it could “further enhance” the travel experience for its customers.

SIA also elaborated on the growth strategy for loss-making Air India, in which it holds a 25.1% stake, noting that the airline is aiming to achieve profitability under new leadership and with growth opportunities emerging in the market.

The company posted $5.6 billion in revenue, 14.3% higher year on year, for the second quarter ended Sept 30. Net profit also quadrupled to $209.7 million.

Despite the strong quarter, the airline’s net profit for the first half of its financial year still fell 43.9% to $134 million, as rising jet fuel prices driven by the Middle East conflict took a toll on its performance.

Jet fuel prices were lower in the second quarter than the first quarter, said group chief financial officer JoAnn Tan.

The surge, however, still led to a 90.3% increase in fuel costs before hedging for the first half of the financial year.

Shares of SIA closed Nov 12 at $7.25, up 1.1%.

Here are the key takeaways from SIA’s results briefing for the first half of its 2027 financial year:

Possible changes to the business-class seat

SIA’s long-haul business-class seats, revealed on Nov 7 alongside refreshed products across all its other cabin classes, has sparked substantial debate.

Central to the discussion were the seat’s shape and grey palette, which drew comparisons to a dental chair, and the bright yellow stripe across the backrest, which critics said strayed too far from the colours traditionally associated with the airline.

The business-class cabin was designed by BMW Group’s Designworks, one of three design studios hired by SIA to design its fleetwide overhaul for $2 billion in total.

Due to launch in the second half of 2027, the seats will be introduced progressively on 41 Airbus A350-900 long-haul and ultra-long-range aircraft as they are retrofitted, as well as on SIA’s upcoming Boeing 777-9 planes. Deliveries of the Boeing aircraft have already been delayed by five years, and the model is still awaiting certification.

SIA has defended the seat’s design following the public outcry and now says it will consider adjustments in response to feedback. A petition on Change.org is calling for the airline to remove the yellow accents.

Asked by The Straits Times whether engaging a single agency for the entire redesign could have produced a more unified look and reduced costs, Goh said the airline’s decision was based on the different requirements of each cabin class.

“What we’ve done is to choose the most appropriate agency for the needs of that specific business class,” he said.

An SIA spokesperson added that the airline has historically hired multiple agencies for its cabin overhauls. This includes the 2017 refresh for its Airbus A380 aircraft, where one design studio was involved in its Suites design and another for the business-class and premium economy seats.

Design studios must comply with both US Federal Aviation Administration and European Union Aviation Safety Agency regulations before they are invited to bid.

The spokesperson added that the $2 billion investment was not a huge sum when compared with SIA’s financials.

Air India pursuing new growth opportunities

A lower share of losses from Air India helped support SIA’s earnings for the second quarter. SIA, which owns a 25.1% stake in Air India, recorded a $361.7 million share of the carrier’s losses, down from $429.5 million a year earlier.

Tan said this was mainly due to a reversal of provisions that SIA had made in previous years, and not because Air India had performed better.

In its next stage of growth, Air India will pursue opportunities within and outside of India, Goh said, adding that the airline has already taken steps to improve revenue generation and cost management under a new CEO.

Tewolde Gebremariam, who is the former CEO of Ethiopian Airlines, officially joined Air India on Oct 1.

Plans include rebalancing Air India’s hubs by shifting the bulk of its Europe- and US-bound flights from Delhi to Mumbai, as well as establishing a third hub in Bengaluru, as a result of the closure of Pakistan’s airspace impacting the airline’s operations.

Moving westbound flights to Mumbai would help to reduce fuel costs due to the shorter flight times, Goh said.

“Gebremariam has also gone out to make sure that Air India is able to beef up its capabilities to sell outside of India,” he added, noting that the airline will be looking to tap the increase in overseas demand for international travel.

There is also a big growth opportunity in the air cargo segment with significant demand in India, which Air India has yet to fully capitalise. On this front, the airline plans to convert some of its passenger aircraft into dedicated freighters.

SIA’s AI transformation

Goh also gave an update on the airline’s digital transformation, stressing that it was taking an “enterprise perspective” by looking at how changes could benefit the company as a whole.

“We haven’t seen any good example of an airline adopting an end-to-end transversal approach to the adoption of AI.

“Usually it’s quite limited to each business unit and progressing from each business unit, we feel that is not a strong enough approach because in the airline industry, all our functions are interlinked.”

According to Goh, AI solutions have been deployed in numerous facets of the business, from raising its workforce productivity to increasing customer and revenue generation. It has seen a 67% year-on-year increase in AI use cases, which have already improved areas such as its customer insights portal, crew scheduling and cabin crew training.

Goh said the company-wide AI transformation is an ambitious project, requiring SIA to partner with leading AI companies, including ChatGPT developer OpenAI and Muse, Meta’s AI agent for agentic commerce.

“When we say collaborate, we are not talking about buying solutions but working alongside our partners and exploring what opportunities we can actually bring in with the use of these generative AI tools.”

data.title: Nvidia lost its founding CEO. Can it keep its momentum?
data.description:
Advice to Nvidia’s board: choose a techie.

As the chip giant’s directors seek a replacement to Jensen Huang, the history of successions at Silicon Valley companies suggests that the odds of long-term success are better with a person steeped in technology and product development rather than finance, sales or marketing.

Replacing a founder is a defining moment for any company, whether it has been planned for years or is a sudden departure; whether the company is thriving or faltering.

For Huang, Nvidia’s co-founder and former chief executive officer, the fall came remarkably quickly. He resigned on Nov 12 after the disclosure of affairs with a woman identified by US intelligence as a Chinese spy and with an executive who reported to him.

Nvidia’s business as the leading chip supplier to artificial intelligence data centres is flourishing. Huang’s hasty exit, analysts say, will have little near-term effect on the company’s business, despite a big stock-market reaction – the company’s shares have fallen 14% in the past five days.

But the best tech leaders steer their companies towards opportunity. At Nvidia, founded in 1993, Huang recognised more than a decade ago that chips used mainly for image-processing in computer games could be repurposed as the hardware engines for AI software. It was a huge bet for the small company – and paid off.

“You can coast on the founder’s work for years with good execution,” said Steve Blank, a Silicon Valley entrepreneur and investor, who is an adjunct professor at Stanford University. “But you can lack the founder’s vision to see over the horizon and identify what’s next. That’s why the best successors have a lot of technical acumen as well as business acumen.”

Over the years, the results for tech companies replacing founding executives have been decidedly mixed.

In 1985, Apple co-founder Steve Jobs was forced out after clashing with his CEO, John Sculley, who had come from Pepsico.

Under Sculley, Apple enjoyed years of rising profits. But the company eventually struggled to compete against lower-cost personal computers based on Microsoft’s Windows software and Intel’s microprocessors. Scully left Apple in 1993.

Three years later, with Apple’s survival uncertain, Jobs returned and became CEO. A renowned product team leader, he led a corporate renaissance, introducing new digital devices including the iPod and the iPhone that transformed the product categories of music players and cellphones.

In 2011, shortly before he died, Jobs named Tim Cook as his successor. Cook has a degree in industrial engineering as well as a master’s in business administration (MBA). While some analysts said Apple lost some of its innovative spark, today the company is valued at US$5.16 trillion (S$6.64 trillion), the most valuable in the world.

In September, Cook became executive chair and John Ternus, a mechanical engineer and product development executive, became the company’s CEO.

Intel did not fare so well. While Andrew Grove did not found the chipmaker, he was among its first employees and led the company for nearly two decades. Grove emigrated from Hungary, learnt English and earned an undergraduate degree and a doctorate in chemical engineering.

Grove led Intel’s drive to dominate the market for microprocessor chips, the electronic brains of personal computers. He became the face of Intel and one of the architects of the personal computer industry, named Time magazine’s Man Of The Year in 1997.

Grove’s immediate successor in 1998, Craig Barrett, was also a technologist. But later successors were less so – and Intel’s fortunes declined precipitously. As part of efforts to help revive American chip manufacturing, the US government said in 2025 that it would invest nearly US$9 billion in Intel for a stake of just under 10%.

Some of the biggest tech companies have learnt that technical expertise at the top is indispensable. Bill Gates, co-founder of Microsoft, stepped aside as CEO in 2000 and handed the job to his long-time business partner, Steve Ballmer.

Ballmer was known as a brilliant sales and business development executive, and a tireless, hands-on manager. During his years as CEO, from 2000 to 2014, Microsoft’s sales and profits rose steadily.

But Ballmer’s lack of tech expertise contributed to an erosion of Microsoft’s reputation as an industry leader. Big-spending initiatives, especially trying to compete with Apple in smartphone software and hardware, failed.

Satya Nadella, who holds undergraduate and graduate degrees in computer science, as well as an MBA, succeeded Ballmer in 2014. Nadella quickly refocused the company.

“He recognised that the future for Microsoft was not going to be mobile,” said David Yoffie, a professor at the Harvard Business School. “It was going to be the cloud. And he very effectively drove the company in that direction.”

Today, Microsoft is a leading provider of cloud computing services, its software programmes are available on the cloud, and it is investing heavily in AI. The company is valued at US$3.88 trillion.

For Nvidia, its next leader is going to have to chart a long-term strategy. With a 90% share of the current market for advanced AI chips and cash flooding in, the company will be able to bankroll its next moves.

Still, Nvidia’s very market dominance invites competition. Google, for example, has developed chips designed for AI. And companies in the United States and China are working on open-source alternatives to CUDA – Nvidia’s software platform for its chips – that are free to use and modify.

The CUDA software, used by an estimated four million developers, reinforces Nvidia’s grip on the market. Nvidia’s current business is racing along.

“But the company has not really mapped out and articulated a future yet,” said Michael Cusumano, a professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology’s Sloan School of Management.

The travails of Huang, 63, are also evidence that he was not as laser-focused on the business as he once was, Cusumano said. Seeing the next AI market turn could take fresh eyes.

“Jensen Huang has done an incredible job over the years, but it may not be a bad time to replace him,” Cusumano added. NYTIMES

data.title: Trade US stocks like digital tokens soon?
data.description:
The accelerating drive to turn listed company stocks into digital tokens risks introducing crypto-like dangers into the US equity market with few benefits. The potential drawbacks include money laundering, insider trading and even theft – as the recent US$6.3 billion (S$8.1 billion) Binance Holdings hack shows. The only winners would be trading platforms hunting for extra income.

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) ploughed ahead with efforts to promote tokenised securities – digital entries of rights or ownership in shares, recorded on a blockchain or distributed ledger – in September, suspending many rules and investor protections for firms trying to develop the market.

data.title: US equities close lower as Nvidia drop outweighs energy gains
data.description:
NEW YORK - US stocks closed lower on Nov 12, as a drop in Nvidia shares after CEO Jensen Huang’s exit outweighed gains in energy shares.

The chip company’s shares fell but were well off the day’s lowest level after earlier dropping nearly 12%.

Retail investors bought Nvidia shares worth about US$111 million (S$142 million) in the first half hour of trading, the biggest opening bid on record for the stock, according to data from Vanda Analytics.

The S&P 500 energy index rose for a fourth straight session as the best-performing of the 11 major S&P sectors. Crude prices climbed after President Donald Trump wrote on social media that the US did not need a deal with Iran.

Global AI-linked stocks fell and AI cloud firm Nebius tumbled after reporting its quarterly earnings and outlook. But Nvidia competitors such as Broadcom, Advanced Micro Devices, Alphabet and Amazon moved higher and were among the biggest boosts to the S&P 500.

Equities have been volatile in recent days. Sweeping Democratic victories in the US midterm elections have sparked investor concern about more AI regulation. Worries about Nvidia’s leadership have also pressured one of the foundations of the current bull market. Nvidia tabbed chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO.

“Right now, the market is selling AI stocks and tech stocks and buying safe stuff, just like it did in the first halo trade in January and February of this year, but it will flip back,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management in St Louis.

“That’s the tug of war the market is doing right now. It’s concerns about deceleration versus just pointing out that the absolute valuation and growth rates are still pretty compelling.”

According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 lost 25.99 points, or 0.34%, to end at 7,593.39 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 102.44 points, or 0.40%, to 25,363.75.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 190.29 points, or 0.36%, to 52,296.20.

Nvidia financing scrutiny

Even with Huang’s departure, some investors expect questions to persist about the future of AI companies with strong ties to Nvidia.

The company has backed several firms, including its own customers, through financing arrangements that face greater scrutiny after Huang’s departure.

“Nvidia is the circular-funder-in-chief; they’re the biggest by far at this point, and I assume that activity will moderate,” said Ellerbroek.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor index declined after surging 17.2% over the prior four sessions.

Along with Nebius, peer CoreWeave dropped. Shares of data centre-related firms IREN and Applied Digital also slumped.

Investors await inflation data

Investors are awaiting the release of the Producer Price Index on Nov 13, which will follow a hotter-than-expected consumer price reading earlier this week.

Markets are completely pricing in a December rate hike of at least 25 basis points by the Federal Reserve, with a 15% chance of a 50-basis-point increase, according to CME FedWatch.

Comments from multiple Fed officials earlier this week suggested the US central bank was open to a more aggressive path of rate hikes as price pressures worsen.

Cleveland Fed president Beth Hammack said on Nov 12 she does not believe the central bank needs to shift to more aggressive rate hikes to combat inflation, while San Francisco Federal Reserve president Mary Daly said she thinks the central bank will likely need to raise interest rates further to deal with elevated inflation, but did not suggest any urgency. REUTERS

data.title: Microsoft outage hits MAS, banks’ e-mails; banks offer customers alternative contact channels
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Banks in Singapore whose e-mails and communications have been affected by the global Microsoft outage have reached out to customers with alternative ways to access help, including customer service hotlines and relationship managers.

Meanwhile, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said it was closely monitoring the situation. The financial regulator has also experienced disruption to its e-mail services, but said its operations remained unaffected.

The Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS) said banks affected by the disruption, particularly those providing retail banking services, have put up notices on various channels, including their websites, to alert customers to the outage.

Checks by The Straits Times show that DBS, UOB, OCBC, HSBC and Maybank Singapore are among those affected.

ABS director Ong-Ang Ai Boon said banks were making alternative contact arrangements available to customers while the disruption persisted.

Customers are advised not to click on unknown or unsolicited links or respond to messages relating to the disruption as these could lead to phishing attempts, scams, credential theft and malware infections.

The advisory comes amid concerns that cybercriminals could take advantage of the disruption to impersonate banks or send fraudulent messages to customers seeking information or help.

DBS, Singapore’s largest lender, said responses to e-mails would be delayed because of the Microsoft outage. DBS customers can, however, continue to perform transactions via the bank’s ATMs, debit/credit cards, DBS/POSB digibank and PayLah!, all of which remain unaffected.

They can use DBS/POSB digibank to receive push notifications.

DBS wealth and corporate clients can also contact their relationship managers.

The bank also warned customers to beware of scammers claiming to be from DBS or technology companies offering to resolve system issues.

Maybank Singapore said in a Facebook post that all its digital and physical banking services remain safe and operational, though e-mails may be delayed. It directed customers to its digital channels, ATMs and self-service terminals.

OCBC said responses to customer inquiries may be delayed. Those requiring urgent help should reach out to their relationship managers or the bank’s customer service hotlines.

It too reminded customers to be vigilant against scammers taking advantage of the disruption.

Microsoft suffered a major global outage, bringing many of its widely used tools, including e-mail and cloud storage, to a standstill. In Singapore, Downdetector began recording reports at about 2am overnight, with numbers continuing to climb on the morning of Nov 13.

MAS, in a banner displayed on its website, said it was monitoring its systems and the broader situation closely.

Members of the public can continue to contact the central bank through its online feedback form.

Financial institutions seeking to reach MAS can also use alternative channels, including phone calls or the online feedback form, it added.

data.title: Haze-linked First Resources, Bumitama post higher profits for Q3
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Two palm oil companies linked to the transboundary haze in October reported higher profits for the third quarter ended Sept 30, in separate business updates published on the morning of Nov 13.

Palm oil producer First Resources posted a 40.1% rise in its underlying net profit to US$122.7 million (S$157.9 million) for the third quarter of 2026, from US$87.5 million in the year-ago period.

The increase was boosted by higher sales of palm oil products and fruit bunches harvested from oil palms, it said.

Sales were up 24.9% at US$578.6 million for the quarter, compared with US$463.3 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation rose 26.6% to US$207.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, up from US$163.8 million a year ago.

For the nine months ended Sept 30, sales grew 36.5% year on year to US$1.6 billion, driven by higher sales volumes.

A net inventory drawdown of 28,000 tonnes over the nine-month period, compared with a build-up of 80,000 tonnes in the corresponding period in 2025, also supported higher sales volumes.

The group’s stronger production output in the first nine months of 2026 was also attributable in part to the full nine-month contribution from Austindo Nusantara Jaya, an Indonesian agribusiness company acquired in May 2025.

However, profits were partially offset by foreign currency translation losses resulting from the depreciation of the Indonesian rupiah against the US dollar.

The group said it expects demand for palm oil to remain supported by Indonesia’s biodiesel programme.

In addition, elevated crude oil prices arising from geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are expected to support biodiesel economics and crude palm oil demand.

Performance supported by productivity improvements

Meanwhile, Bumitama reported a 1.9% increase in its net profit to 614.1 billion rupiah (S$43.4 million) for the quarter ended Sept 30, compared with 602.9 billion rupiah in the previous corresponding period.

For the nine-month period, net profit rose 30.6% to 2.4 trillion rupiah, up from 1.9 trillion rupiah in the year-ago period.

Revenue increased 9.7% to 4.2 trillion rupiah in the third quarter, up from 3.9 trillion rupiah a year ago. For the nine-month period, revenue was up 20% at 16.3 trillion rupiah.

Bumitama said its performance was supported by productivity improvements in its plantations and mills, particularly during the earlier part of the quarter.

In July, internal production of fresh fruit bunches reached 383,203 tonnes, accounting for almost 40% of the quarter’s production.

Quarterly production of crude palm oil increased 14% year on year to 368,323 tonnes.

However, exceptionally dry weather conditions in its Kalimantan estates during the third quarter put additional pressure on logistics infrastructure and disrupted shipments, said Bumitama.

Consequently, third-quarter revenue declined compared with the second quarter.

The prolonged dry season also heightened the risk of land and forest fires across parts of Kalimantan.

Fires affected certain areas within or adjoining the group’s concessions, including community-managed, conservation and unplanted land, the group noted.

Bumitama said that elevated energy prices and Indonesia’s biodiesel programme coupled with a relatively constrained palm oil supply growth could provide a “supportive backdrop” for palm oil fundamentals heading into 2027.

However, market conditions remain subject to uncertainty.

These include changes in global energy prices, supply-and-demand dynamics, and the potential effects of prolonged dry weather on future production, it added.

Both First Resources and Bumitama reiterated their commitment to upholding a zero-burning policy, and cooperating with the Indonesian and Singapore authorities in relation to the haze.

Shares of First Resources closed at $2.97, up 6.45%, and those of Bumitama closed flat at $1.39 on Nov 13, after the updates. THE BUSINESS TIMES
